'''Henry Shattuck Richardson''' (born 1955)<ref name="thesis">{{cite thesis|last=Richardson|first=Henry Shattuck|url=http://id.lib.harvard.edu/alma/990019874370203941/catalog|title=Rational deliberation of ends|year=1986|type=Ph.D.|publisher=Harvard University}}</ref><ref>{{cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=ejksDwAAQBAJ&q=%22henry+shattuck+richardson%22+1955&pg=PT1010|title=Affirming: Letters 1975-1997|last=Berlin|first=Isaiah|place=New York|publisher=Random House|year=2017|isbn=9781473555396}}</ref> is an American philosopher, author, and professor of philosophy at [[Georgetown University]], where he is also a senior research scholar at the [[Kennedy Institute of Ethics]].<ref name=Georgetown>{{cite web|title=Henry S Richardson|url=http://explore.georgetown.edu/people/richardh/?PageTemplateID=189|publisher=Georgetown University|access-date=13 April 2014}}</ref><ref name=Kennedy>{{cite web|title=Henry S. Richardson, J.D., M.P.P., Ph.D.|url=http://kennedyinstitute.georgetown.edu/ourpeople/richardson.cfm|publisher=Kennedy Institute of Ethics|access-date=13 April 2014|archive-date=8 April 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140408211431/http://kennedyinstitute.georgetown.edu/ourpeople/richardson.cfm|url-status=dead}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Richardson is the son of Anne Richardson, who was once the chair of [[Reading is Fundamental]], and the politician and lawyer [[Elliot Richardson]], who served as [[United States Secretary of Defense]], [[United States Attorney General|Attorney General]], and [[United States Secretary of Commerce|Secretary of Commerce]].<ref name=AnneR>{{cite news|title=Anne Richardson, 69, Patron of Literacy (obituary)|url=https://www.nytimes.com/1999/07/29/us/anne-richardson-69-patron-of-literacy.html|access-date=13 April 2014|newspaper=The New York Times|date=29 July 1999}}</ref>

Richardson graduated ''[[magna cum laude]]'' from [[Harvard University]] with a [[Bachelor of Arts]] degree in 1977. He then received a [[Juris Doctor|J.D.]] from [[Harvard Law School]] and an [[Master of Public Policy|M.P.P.]] from the [[John F. Kennedy School of Government]] (supervised by [[Martha Nussbaum]]), both in 1981. In 1986, Richardson received his [[Ph.D.]] in Philosophy from Harvard University under the supervision of [[John Rawls]]; his thesis was titled ''Rational deliberation of ends''.<ref name=Georgetown /><ref name="thesis"/>

==Academic career==
Richardson's main work has centred on [[practical reasoning]]. His first book, ''Practical Reasoning about Final Ends'',<ref name=Final>{{cite book | last = Richardson | first = Henry | title = Practical reasoning about final ends | publisher = Cambridge University Press | location = Cambridge New York | year = 1997 | isbn = 9780521574426 }}</ref> focused on individual reasoning, whilst his second book, ''Democratic Autonomy: Public Reasoning about the Ends of Policy'',<ref name=Autonomy>{{cite book | last = Richardson | first = Henry | title = Democratic autonomy: public reasoning about the ends of policy | url = https://archive.org/details/democra_ric_2002_00_3028 | url-access = registration | publisher = Oxford University Press | location = New York | year = 2002 | isbn = 9780195150919 }}</ref> which won the [[Herbert A. Simon]] Best Book Award in Public Administration,<ref name=Herbert>{{cite web|title=Organized Section Awards - Public Administration Organized Section: Herbert A. Simon Book Award Recipients|url=http://www.apsanet.org/sections/sectionAwardDetail.cfm?award=SEC06AHSBA|publisher=American Political Science Association|access-date=13 April 2014}}</ref>  and the David Easton Award in the Foundations of Political Theory,<ref name=Easton>{{cite web|title=Book awards: David Easton Award|url=https://www.librarything.com/bookaward/David+Easton+Award|publisher=Library Thing|access-date=13 April 2014}}</ref>  dealt with collective reasoning.

In addition to working on practical reasoning and moral and political philosophy, Richardson has written on [[bioethics]]. He has twice been a visiting scholar at the Department of Bioethics at the (U.S.) National Institutes of Health.

From 2008 to 2018, he was the Editor of the academic journal ''[[Ethics (journal)|Ethics]]''.<ref name=Journal>{{cite web|title=Ethics: An International Journal of Social, Political, and Legal Philosophy (Editorial Board)|url=https://www.jstor.org/journal/ethics|access-date=13 April 2014}}</ref>  From 2010 to 2013, through his work as a member of the World Commission on the Ethics of Scientific Knowledge and Technology (COMEST), he has acted as an advisor to the Director General of [[UNESCO]] on ethical issues relating to science and technology.<ref name=Georgetown /><ref name=Kennedy />

In September 2014 Richardson began a two-year tenure as president of the [[Human Development and Capability Association|Human Development and Capability Association (HDCA)]].<ref name=Election>{{cite web|title=Election results for HDCA Executive Council|url=http://hd-ca.org/news/election-results-for-hdca-executive-council|publisher= [[Human Development and Capability Association]] |access-date=13 April 2014|date=15 May 2013}}</ref> He was succeeded by the economist [[Ravi Kanbur]].<ref name=Election_2>{{cite web|title=New HDCA Executive Council members elected!|url=http://hd-ca.org/news/new-hdca-executive-council-members-elected|publisher= [[Human Development and Capability Association]] |access-date= 21 June 2015 |date=8 June 2015}}</ref>  From 2014 to 2017, he served as one of two "coordinating lead authors" on the orienting normative chapter of the three-volume report of the [[International Panel of Social Progress]],<ref name=International>{{cite web|title=International Panel on Social Progress|url=http://www.ipsp.org|publisher= [[International Panel on Social Progress]] |access-date=6 August 2019|date=}}</ref> ''Rethinking Society for the 21st Century.''<ref name=Rethinking>{{cite book | last = International Panel on Social Progress | title = Rethinking Society for the 21st Century: Report of the International Panel on Social Progress | publisher = Cambridge University Press | location = Cambridge | year = 2018 | isbn = 9781108399579 }}</ref>

In 2019, Richardson was awarded a [[Guggenheim Fellowship]].<ref>{{Cite web | url=https://www.gf.org/fellows/all-fellows/henry-s-richardson/ |title = John Simon Guggenheim Foundation &#124; Henry S. Richardson| work=John Simon Guggenheim Memorial Foundation }}</ref>
